key_insight: Scrap-derived twitch aluminum fillers resisted solidification cracking better than 6061, but worse than 4043 and 5356, while producing considerably harder welds.
engineering_relevance: Twitch scrap could support high-strength welding and additive-manufacturing feedstocks if wire-production defects can be controlled.
method: Produced twitch-derived fillers using a powder-core tubular wire process.
Compared solidification-cracking predictions with Sigmajig weldability tests.
Evaluated cracking resistance and weld hardness against commercial aluminum alloys.
evidence_signal: Sigmajig tests contradicted the predicted superiority of twitch alloys over commercial alloys, although twitch welds exhibited considerably higher hardness.
watch_item: Oxides attributed to powder-core wire production reduced weldability, so composition-based cracking predictions alone may overestimate performance.
paper_title: Solidification Cracking Susceptibility of Welding Fillers Derived from Scrap Aluminum — Part 1: Powder Core Wire Experiments
